
# Load Packages
```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
source("00_requirements.R")
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(lubridate)
library(knitr)
```

# Import Datasets
```{r import-data}
btc_raw <- read.csv(
  "Data/BTC-USD.csv",
  check.names = FALSE
)
sp500_raw <- read.csv(
  "Data/^SPX.csv",
  check.names = FALSE
)
tnx_raw <- read.csv(
  "Data/^TNX.csv",
  check.names = FALSE
)
ief_raw <- read.csv(
  "Data/IEF.csv",
  check.names = FALSE
)
```

# Initial Data Exploration
```{r initial-inspection}
dim(btc_raw)
dim(sp500_raw)
dim(tnx_raw)
dim(ief_raw)
names(btc_raw)

```
# check for missing data
```{r missing-inspection}
missing_summary <- data.frame(
  Dataset = c("Bitcoin", "S&P 500", "Treasury Yield", "IEF"),
  Missing_Values = c(
    sum(is.na(btc_raw)),
    sum(is.na(sp500_raw)),
    sum(is.na(tnx_raw)),
    sum(is.na(ief_raw))
  )
)
kable(
  missing_summary,
  caption = "Missing Values in Original Datasets"
)
```

# Jan 1 2020 to Oct 1 2026

```{r date-filtering}
start_date <- as.Date("2020-01-01")
end_date <- as.Date("2026-10-01")

btc_clean <- btc_clean %>%
  filter(Date >= start_date, Date <= end_date)

sp500_clean <- sp500_clean %>%
  filter(Date >= start_date, Date <= end_date)

tnx_clean <- tnx_clean %>%
  filter(Date >= start_date, Date <= end_date)

ief_clean <- ief_clean %>%
  filter(Date >= start_date, Date <= end_date)
```

# 8. Select Relevant Variables

For the investment performance analysis, we primarily
need the date and adjusted closing price.

The Treasury yield dataset is retained separately
for supplementary interest-rate analysis.

```{r select-variables}
btc_analysis <- btc_clean %>%
  select(Date, Adjusted_Close)

sp500_analysis <- sp500_clean %>%
  select(Date, Adjusted_Close)

ief_analysis <- ief_clean %>%
  select(Date, Adjusted_Close)

tnx_analysis <- tnx_clean %>%
  select(Date, Close)
```

# 9. Convert Daily Observations into Monthly Data

Bitcoin trades every day, whereas the stock and
Treasury markets generally operate on business days.

To make the investment comparisons consistent,
we extract the final available observation
for each calendar month.

```{r monthly-function}
get_monthly_data <- function(data) {

  data %>%
    mutate(
      Month = floor_date(Date, unit = "month")
    ) %>%
    group_by(Month) %>%
    slice_max(
      order_by = Date,
      n = 1,
      with_ties = FALSE
    ) %>%
    ungroup()
}
```

We apply the function to all four datasets.

```{r monthly-datasets}
btc_monthly <- get_monthly_data(btc_analysis)

sp500_monthly <- get_monthly_data(sp500_analysis)

ief_monthly <- get_monthly_data(ief_analysis)

tnx_monthly <- get_monthly_data(tnx_analysis)
```

# 10. Combine the Monthly Datasets

We combine the three investment datasets using
their common calendar months.

This ensures that all three investments are
compared over the same monthly periods.

```{r combine-data}
monthly_combined <- btc_monthly %>%
  select(Month, Bitcoin = Adjusted_Close) %>%
  inner_join(
    sp500_monthly %>%
      select(Month, SP500 = Adjusted_Close),
    by = "Month"
  ) %>%
  inner_join(
    ief_monthly %>%
      select(Month, IEF = Adjusted_Close),
    by = "Month"
  ) %>%
  arrange(Month)

kable(
  head(monthly_combined),
  caption = "First Six Observations of Combined Monthly Data"
)
```

# 11. Examine the Cleaned Datasets

We summarize the cleaned observations and
their date ranges.

```{r cleaned-summary}
cleaned_summary <- data.frame(
  Asset = c("Bitcoin", "S&P 500", "IEF", "Treasury Yield"),

  Observations = c(
    nrow(btc_clean),
    nrow(sp500_clean),
    nrow(ief_clean),
    nrow(tnx_clean)
  ),

  Missing_Values = c(
    sum(is.na(btc_clean)),
    sum(is.na(sp500_clean)),
    sum(is.na(ief_clean)),
    sum(is.na(tnx_clean))
  ),

  First_Date = c(
    min(btc_clean$Date),
    min(sp500_clean$Date),
    min(ief_clean$Date),
    min(tnx_clean$Date)
  ),

  Last_Date = c(
    max(btc_clean$Date),
    max(sp500_clean$Date),
    max(ief_clean$Date),
    max(tnx_clean$Date)
  )
)

kable(
  cleaned_summary,
  caption = "Summary of Cleaned Financial Datasets"
)
```

# 12. Save the Cleaned Datasets

Finally, we save the cleaned daily and monthly
datasets for use in subsequent analysis.

```{r save-data}
dir.create("Output", showWarnings = FALSE)

save(
  btc_clean,
  sp500_clean,
  tnx_clean,
  ief_clean,
  btc_monthly,
  sp500_monthly,
  tnx_monthly,
  ief_monthly,
  monthly_combined,
  file = "Output/cleaned_data.RData"
)

write.csv(
  monthly_combined,
  "Output/monthly_combined.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

# 13. Conclusion

The four financial datasets have been imported,
inspected, cleaned, and converted into monthly
observations.

The three investment datasets have also been
combined using their common calendar months.

The resulting datasets are now prepared for
the next stage of the analysis: calculating
investment returns and comparing portfolio
performance.
